text:
Minnesota ended Washington's three-game winning streak with a 5-1 win that was much closer than the score. The Wild's night turned on Jesper Wallstedt, a goalie the Wild drafted 20th overall in 2021 out of Luleå HF, who stopped 26 of 27 shots. Our numbers say he saved about 2.3 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved, which is the gap between a good night and the one that decided this game.

Washington played the better hockey for long stretches. The Capitals edged Minnesota in total chance quality, 3.29 expected goals (a measure of how good the shots were) to 3.25, and in a simulation of every shot replayed, they win this game 56 percent of the time. The second period was theirs, 1.57 to 0.74, and Justin Sourdif tipped one in with 6 seconds left in the period to make it 2-1. Jack St. Ivany had a 25 percent look in that period that Wallstedt turned away. Then Minnesota pulled away late. Maxim Shabanov scored on the power play in the 17th minute of the third, Kirill Kaprizov made it 4-1 on a 5 percent chance for his 500th career point, and Danila Yurov added a power-play goal with 25 seconds left. Quinn Hughes opened the scoring at 3:42 of the first and logged 29:42, and David Spacek picked up his first NHL point, an assist on the Yurov goal.

The Wild leave with a lopsided win built on goaltending and a late burst, and the Capitals have to start a new streak after losing for the first time in four games. Washington took 20 penalty minutes to Minnesota's 2, and the two late power-play goals decided how big the margin became.
